arrow.description: Double-lined arrow with a hatched head, about 66 px from the foot of the shaft to the tip, drawn on the graph paper with the letter N below it. The left shaft line is exactly parallel to the graph-paper verticals; we use the axis from the middle of the shaft foot to the tip.

sources.notes: Hand drawing on graph paper. Black double lines mark the wall exposed in trenches, dashed lines the conjectured course of the fortification, blue outlines the excavated trenches. The graph paper's ruled axes are square to each other within 0.1 deg and turned 0.3 deg on the scan.

systems.description: All exposed stretches of the fort wall; the north-western and north-eastern arms meet at about 92 degrees

main_system_reason: The fort wall is the only measurable Harappan architecture on the plan; its two long exposed arms are square to each other within about two degrees and the shorter stretches on the other two sides agree with them within a few degrees.
notes: We measured the plan of the Harappan fort in Kharakwal et al.'s Nichibunken paper (Fig. 5), a drawing on graph paper with a double-lined north arrow lettered N and a stated scale of 2 cm to 5 m. The fort is set obliquely, its arms running roughly north-east and south-east, about thirty degrees from the cardinal directions. Black double lines mark the wall where exposed; the dashed conjectured course was not measured. The two long arms (north-west and north-east) are exposed for most of their length and meet at about 92 degrees; the short stretches on the south-east and south-west sides are less certain. The arrow is drawn along the graph paper and its shaft is parallel to the ruled verticals within about one degree, so the plan's north is the graph-paper north of the drawing. The final report (Kharakwal et al. 2012, RIHN) is not available to us; the locally held chapter 8 has no plan.
